finding.expected: Make next_run_id() recognize the complete canonical numeric RUN suffix grammar used by remote namespace validation so every valid reserved/local identity, including 1000 and above, participates in allocation. Add deterministic boundary regressions proving a namespace containing 001 through 1000 allocates 1001 rather than reusing 1000, including coverage sufficient to prove the shared allocator protects normal admission and recover-primary. Preserve all existing remote validation, conflict detection, Executor/no-Executor, Runtime verification, and publication semantics.
finding.issue: Canonical remote namespace validation accepts task-bound RUN identities with a numeric suffix of three or more digits, but next_run_id() still parses local and reserved RUN ids using exactly three digits. Once canonical history reaches RUN-<TASK>-1000, that valid remote reservation is ignored by the allocator. With RUN-<TASK>-001 through RUN-<TASK>-1000 present remotely and fresh/empty local Runtime state, the recognized maximum remains 999 and next_run_id() returns the already-canonical RUN-<TASK>-1000. The same allocator is shared by PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, direct-candidate, REPAIR, and recover-primary, so the defect violates the task's no-reuse guarantee and can also make collision recovery allocate a non-fresh identity.
